'''Gideon Jan (Don) Mellenbergh''' (9 August 1938 – 27 March 2021) was a Dutch [[psychologist]], who was Professor of [[Psychological Methods|Psychological methods]] at the [[University of Amsterdam]], known for his contribution in the field of [[psychometrics]],<ref>Raegan Murphy (2001) ''Dynamic Assessment, Intelligence and Measurement''. p. 106</ref><ref>Frank Columbus (2001) ''Advances in Psychology Research''. Vol 6. p. 55</ref> and [[Social research#Methodology|Social Research Methodology]].

== Biography ==
Born and raised in [[Amsterdam]], Mellenbergh received his MA in psychology from the University of Amsterdam in 1965, and his PhD in psychology in 1971 under the supervision of Professor [[Adriaan de Groot]] with a dissertation about [[Test (assessment)|educational tests]], entitled "Studies in studietoetsen" (Studies on educational tests).<ref name="GJM CV" >[http://www.uva.nl/over-de-uva/organisatie/medewerkers/content/m/e/g.j.mellenbergh/g.j.mellenbergh.html dhr. prof.dr. G.J. (Don) Mellenbergh], Vitae. University of Amsterdam, Accessed May 18, 2013</ref>

At the University of Amsterdam, Mellenbergh began his academic career as an assistant professor of psychological methods in 1965. Late 1969 he was visiting research assistant at the [[University of Chicago]], studying educational methods. From 1975 to 1978 he was Associate professor [[Psychometrics]] at the [[University of Utrecht]], and then returned to the University of Amsterdam where he was Professor, Psychological Methods from 1982 to 2003. Among his PhD students were [[Henk Koppelaar]] and [[Denny Borsboom]]. In 1991 and 1993 he had been Visiting professor at the [[University of Santiago de Compostela]], Spain.<ref name="GJM CV"/>

Mellenbergh performed many administrative functions in Dutch research institutes, is member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (KNAW) since 1993,<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/4543 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200603193050/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/4543 |title=Don Mellenbergh |language=Dutch |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=3 June 2020}}</ref> the [[Psychometric Society]], the [[American Psychological Association]] (APA), the [[International Statistical Institute]] (ISI), and the Interuniversity Graduate School of Psychometrics and Sociometrics (IOPS). And Mellenbergh was editor at [[Psychometrika]], on the editorial Board of ''Psychological Methods'' and member of the editorial council of ''[[Psicothema]]''.<ref name="GJM CV"/>

He died on 27 March 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iops.nl/uncategorized/in-memoriam-don-mellenbergh/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210418055116/https://www.iops.nl/uncategorized/in-memoriam-don-mellenbergh/ |title=In memoriam Don Mellenbergh |publisher= Interuniversity graduate school of Psychometrics and Sociometrics |date=7 April 2021 |archive-date=18 April 2021}}</ref>

== Publications ==
Books and papers, a selection:
* 1970. ''An Application of a Model of Rasch''
* 1999. ''Research Methodology in the Social, Behavioural and Life Sciences''. With [[Herman J. Ader]]
* 2008 ''[https://books.google.com/books?id=LCnOj4ZFyjkC Advising on Research Methods: a consultant's companion].'' With [[Herman J. Adèr]] and [[David Hand (statistician)|David J. Hand]] (eds.). Johannes van Kessel Publ. p.&nbsp;244.
* 2011. ''A Conceptual Introduction to Psychometrics''

Articles, a selection:
* [[Flier, H.]], Mellenbergh, G. J., [[Adèr, H. J.]], & Wijn, M. (1984). An iterative item bias detection method. Journal of educational measurement, 21(2), 131-145.
